elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience (Agreement and/or Order Form)
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor"
"Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term"
"upon 30 days' prior written notice" (30 days, better than fallback but not the 60–90 day figure)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; insertion contains only a refund obligation

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" — no end-of-term Vendor right granted

reasons: All four atomic preferred elements are present in the single inserted Section 9.4: Customer convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata in substance), and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.

The "Notwithstanding Section 2.1" opener is necessary rather than surplus, because Section 2.1 purports to remove termination rights; without it the new right would conflict with the take-or-pay commitment.

Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (notice is 30 rather than 60–90 days, no early-termination fee, no end-of-term Vendor convenience right), but the levels are separate bargains and the locked target is preferred.
Minimality holds: a concise single-paragraph insertion for an absent clause, numbered 9.4 in sequence, with no rewriting of Sections 9.1–9.5 and no new exceptions or duplicated protections.

Intent preserved: the take-or-pay volume commitment, breach, insolvency, and cause-termination rights and the Order Form survival mechanic in 8.1 remain effective, and no undefined term is introduced ("Fees", "Order Form" are defined; "committed term" reads against the three-year commitment in 2.1/8.1).
